item.title: Let local communities be the stewards of their own wildlife | Letter
item.summary: Sjúrður Hammer responds to NatureScot’s decision to prohibit the annual guga hunt, where islanders collect gannet chicks on the Hebridean island of Sula Sgeir What many celebrate as a win for nature conservation is, in my view, a significant step in the wrong direction for our relationship with the natural world ( Scottish gannet chick hunt blocked for first time in 400 years, 3 August ). The decision to prohibit the community on Lewis from collecting gannets runs counter to the spirit of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which recognises that safeguarding biodiversity will not be achieved by scientists and city dwellers alone. Instead, it affirms that indigenous and local communities hold a legitimate and essential role as stewards and caretakers of their own environments. Too often, people in our part of the world assume that “indigenous and local communities” refers only to distant, exotic cultures or to the shameful legacies of colonialism.
